properties.title: Titanic maiden voyage
properties.why_famous: The best-known ocean-liner disaster, which drove major changes in maritime safety.
properties.route_summary: Southampton–Cherbourg–Queenstown (Cobh)–Titanic wreck site; New York was the intended destination, not a reached port.
properties.source_title: Royal Museums Greenwich: Titanic facts and voyage timeline
properties.geometry_note: Three embarkation ports and the southern liner track's approximate 42°N, 47°W turning area are documented by the British inquiry; Titanic continued roughly 10 miles southwest before altering course. The plotted turn is a regional estimate, not an observed fix. The final point is NOAA's surveyed bow wreck position, not necessarily the exact impact or sinking surface position. Other ocean controls remain illustrative; New York was not reached.

additional_sources.title: British Wreck Commissioner's Inquiry: findings on Titanic's route
additional_sources.note: Identifies the outward southern track and approximate course alteration near 42°N, 47°W; the plotted offset is an estimate.
